messages:
incident-bot: PAGE [SEV2] - elevated 502s observed in eu-south for service="gateway-proxy". Pager: maya (oncall). Incident ID INC-2051236789. Please acknowledge and start mitigation.

maya (oncall): ack. I'm on it. scope? which customers/paths impacted?

jonah (runtime): I'm seeing a large cluster of 502s originating from gateway -> cache-proxy (eu-south). Quick metrics: gateway_5xx_rate[5m] ~ 0.18 (18%), gateway_latency_p95 ~ 1200ms. Logs show repeated "upstream reset by peer" and "cache eviction in progress" entries. Tracing indicates requests timing out at cache tier ~500ms then gateway returns 502.

maya (oncall): ok — is this an origin/backing service problem or the cache layer itself?

jonah (runtime): looks like cache eviction flood. Node memory pressure triggered LRU eviction and an eviction background job started at ~2051236700. Then many cache-miss stalls triggered synchronous fetches to origin, origin handles spiky fanout poorly => client timeouts. Also saw spikes of TCP RST to cache-proxy from a subset of instances.

leah (platform): adding some context — automated cache-eviction tuning was rolled out yesterday (canary) to reduce mem retention. Might be correlated. Config: cache/eviction_policy=aggressive. We can rollback that config or shift traffic away from eu-south to reduce load.

iris (support): customers reporting increased 502s for chat endpoints in EU. CS ticket volume rising. Notifying top customers now.

maya (oncall): immediate mitigation options: 1) apply routing override to route eu-south -> eu-west for new traffic; 2) roll back eviction policy; 3) scale up cache-proxy pool in eu-south. Which is fastest?

jonah (runtime): fastest is (1) route override. (3) may help but takes autoscaling time. (2) requires config rollout and might be slower depending on CI gating.

maya (oncall): ok. @leah can you push routing override? Need minimal blast radius and TTL of 30m.

leah (platform): on it. applying route override via traffic-config patch.

leah (platform): command I'm running:
```
kubectl -n infra patch configmap traffic-config -p '{"data":{"regional_routing":"eu-south:priority=low, fallback=eu-west,ttl=1800"}}'
```
Expect control plane to pick up in ~30s. I'll post when active.

deploy-bot: traffic-config updated by leah (platform) (rev: cfg-2026-03-15-8). Change propagated to control plane in 22s.

jonah (runtime): confirming: I can see the route policy applied in /controlplane/routes: eu-south -> split 20% local, 80% eu-west (temporary). Starting to drain new connections to problematic cache nodes.

maya (oncall): monitoring metrics now.

maya (oncall): gateway_5xx_rate dropped from 18% -> 6% over last 3 minutes. p95 latency down to 420ms. Looks promising.

iris (support): updating customers: "We've applied a temporary routing change to reduce errors in EU — engineers are mitigating, will follow up with root cause and timeline." :thumbsup:

jonah (runtime): additional note: I found these logs on cache-proxy pods showing eviction loop and OOM-kill attempts. snippet:
```
2026-03-15T10:12:34Z cache-proxy-3 stderr: memwatch: free=120MB limit=256MB -> triggering eviction
2026-03-15T10:12:35Z cache-proxy-3 stderr: eviction: removed 1200 keys in 1s
2026-03-15T10:12:36Z cache-proxy-3 stderr: connection-reset upstream=origin-1 (RST)
```
Looks like aggressive eviction causes an immediate spike in origin fetches which floods origin and causes resets.

leah (platform): rollback plan for eviction policy prepared. Rolling it back would require a config bump and a quick restart of cache-proxy daemonset (controlled restart). We need to coordinate to avoid creating more origin pressure.

maya (oncall): do we need to coordinate with origin team? If origin is the bottleneck, routing to eu-west only buys time.

jonah (runtime): origin appears to be strained by sudden fanout. We should throttle fanout if we rollback eviction — i.e., a staged rollout and increase cache-proxy replicas first.

leah (platform): can scale cache-proxy in eu-south by +3 replicas immediately. Doing kubectl scale now.

leah (platform): command: kubectl -n services scale deploy/cache-proxy-eu-south --replicas=10

deploy-bot: scale triggered by leah (platform) -> cache-proxy-eu-south replicas: 7 -> 10. Pods scheduling.

maya (oncall): good. monitor origin and gateway. If errors continue after routing change + scale, we'll rollback eviction.

(5m later)

maya (oncall): metrics look stable. gateway_5xx_rate ~2.1%, p95 300ms. New errors are minimal.

iris (support): CS update: "Issue mitigated: we routed traffic and scaled cache layer; investigating root cause. ETA for RCA: 24h." Customers acknowledged.

jonah (runtime): collecting heap profiles and eviction histograms for RCA. Will dump them to S3: s3://redwood-inference/inc/2051236789/

leah (platform): creating follow-up ticket and postmortem checklist. Actions: revert aggressive eviction rollout, add circuit-breaker on cache-proxy->origin fanout, add admission throttle to limit concurrent origin fetches on cold miss, and improve observability for eviction storms.

maya (oncall): handing off to jonah for post-incident investigation. I'll remain on rotation for follow-ups, but marking on-call handover.

jonah (runtime): taking ownership for RCA and mitigations. Timeline: initial analysis + heap/profile upload within 3h, postmortem draft by EOD.

maya (oncall): incident timeline summary to include in report: start 2051236789 (page), routing override at 2051236805, scale to 10 at 2051236840, error rate restored by 2051237000. Closing incident channel when stable for 30m.

deploy-bot: Monitoring alert cleared for INC-2051236789: gateway_5xx_rate back to normal thresholds.

maya (oncall): thanks everyone. Adding runbook tasks to ticket and will schedule a follow-up meeting with platform and runtime teams. :white_check_mark:

end of thread: will archive after postmortem.
